title: Developer vibe codes Windows 11 alternative operating system for amd64, arm64, and riscv64 hardware
summary: There’s a new vibe-coded OS in town going by the name of LiberNT.
body: There’s a new vibe-coded OS in town going by the name of LiberNT . Its name provides a big clue to its nature: Liber (free), NT (New Technology architecture, as in Windows NT ). As it has been released under GNU’s GPL3.0 license, LiberNT also provides a free new way to run apps designed for Microsoft’s Windows 11 . (Image credit: LiberNT ) LiberNT has been under development for some time, but on Wednesday it made a big leap. Reading the intro, you might have wondered if this work had a ReactOS connection, and indeed there is. But what started as a fork of ReactOS has already got a new boot loader, graphics stack, memory manager – and yesterday a new kernel . “LiberNT is not affiliated with or endorsed by the ReactOS project or Microsoft,” insist the devs behind this OS. This still fledgling operating system is designed (mostly) for modern hardware and focuses on 64-bit platforms: amd64, arm64 and riscv64. title: Intel 18A yields hit 70% as company signs Microsoft as EMIB customer
summary: Intel's 18A yields achieve an important milestone as the company signs a long-term Xeon supply deal and EMIB usage agreement with Microsoft.
body: Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, said on Thursday that yields of chips made using the company's latest 18A (1.8nm-class) fabrication process have achieved 70%, which is more or less in line with what one would expect from an all-new manufacturing technology at this stage of its ramp. In addition, Intel and Microsoft have signed an agreement under which Microsoft will secure Intel Xeon supply capacity for years to come and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for in-house silicon. "When I took over [as CEO in March, 2025], 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%," Lip-Bu Tan said at the TomorrowX conference (via @firesidealpha ). Lip-Bu Tan did not specify whether he meant functional yield, parametric yield, or percentage of sellable silicon. However, it is reasonable to expect a CEO of a semiconductor company to talk about functional die yield, the percentage of dies that pass basic electrical and functional testing. title: Pakistan undersea cable fault causes internet failure near Strait of Hormuz
summary: Pakistan's telecommunications authority has confirmed that an undersea network cable fault is behind internet connectivity issues in the country, adding that Transworld Associates is looking into what caused the issue and when it expects it to be fixed. Traffic has been rerouted in the interim.
body: Pakistan's telecommunications authority, the PTA, has confirmed that internet connectivity issues affecting the country's residents are related to the failure of an international submarine cable. SEA-ME-WE 5 is located almost seven miles off the coast of Pakistan, near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, and connects the region with European networks via the Middle East. The TWA says that the outage may have caused intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality, with Transworld Associates (TWA) working to identify the cause of the issue. No timeframe has been provided for when a fix will be available yet, but for now, internet traffic has been rerouted to minimize the impact of the outage. The outage comes weeks after the Islamic Republic of Iran described several undersea fiber cables that run through the Strait of Hormuz as "legitimate new targets" in the ongoing tensions in the area. title: Silicon Motion demos SM8466 PCIe 6.0 SSD controller, expected to ship by 2028 — controller boasts improved quality of service, samples imminent
summary: Silicon Motion's SM8466 has finally taped out and is set to enter the market in 2027-2028.
body: Silicon Motion is showing off its PCIe 6.0 SSD controller for data center applications for the first time at the SC26 conference in Chicago . The final iteration of Silicon Motion's SM8466 controller was taped out recently, and drives based on the chip are due in late 2027 or early 2028. However, the new controller also has a secret weapon designed to ensure consistent performance of SSDs under concurrent workloads that may set it apart from competitors. The new controller Silicon Motion introduced its high-end MonTitan SM8466 enterprise SSD controller designed for next-generation data center and hyperscale storage applications at FMS 2025 . The controller features a PCIe 6.x x4 host interface and 16 NAND channels to enable sequential transfer speeds of up to 28 GB/s, random performance of up to 7 million 4K IOPS, and capacities of up to 512 TB and beyond as newer 3D NAND devices emerge. Just like other high-end data center-grade SSD controllers released in recent years, the SM8466 complies with NVMe 2.0 and OCP NVMe 2.5 SSD specifications. summary: Fugaku, Japan's most powerful supercomputer, has suffered a suspected data breach, with the information of more than 4,000 of its users potentially stolen as a result.
body: Fugaku, Japan's most powerful supercomputer and the ninth-fastest on the planet, has suffered a suspected data breach. The news was announced by its operator, Riken, which is the country's national research institute, with the outfit also confirming that personal information relating to more than 4,000 users of Fugaku was potentially taken during the breach. Further, the information of 375 users of Riken's Rikyu AI supercomputer was also possibly taken. The personal information includes names, email addresses, research files, and even the authentication information that was used to access the supercomputers and related services. The Japan Times reports that the operators of Fugaku first became aware of suspicious communications on November 12, with those suspicions then triggering an investigation. By November 14, the investigation had confirmed that unauthorized access to Fugaku had taken place, with access also blocked at that time. The investigation identified that hackers had used the supercomputer's externally accessible operational status dashboard as the springboard for the hack between November 10 and November 13.
